newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Dell sees strong server sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Dell sees strong server sales.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp Chairman Michael Dell said on Tuesday he expected server sales to continue their rapid growth.

He told Reuters in an interview that, compared to the third quarter, server sales jumped 76 percent in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997, which ended Feb. 2, and now made up 6 percent of overall revenues.
"I think the server momentum is going to continue. We're going to continue to be very aggressive in servers. This is a major area of share gain for us," he said.
Dell earlier reported earnings of $1.01 per share in the fourth quarter, well above last year's $0.35.
Dell said he was not concerned about rival Compaq Computer Corp's recent announcement that it would sell a $999 computer using a chip produced by Cyrix Corp rather than Intel Corp.

"It's kind of like the car with no tires. If you read the press release (from Compaq), you have to get down to the fifth page and it finally tells it doesn't include a monitor. Small detail," he said.
Dell said the inexpensive Compaq machine could end up producing more Dell customers.

"If they bring more first time buyers into the market, it helps us because the second time they buy, they're more likely to go direct," he said, referring to Dell's strategy of selling directly to buyers and not going through a retailer.
He said that Dell was unlikely to try to match the low-priced Compaq. "We play more at the higher end and mid-range. The lower end (of the market) is not really a major space for us," Dell said.
